Only the bottom corners D and E (outlined) have odd degree, so the Eulerian path runs from one to the other, using each of the eight edges once; edges are numbered in the order the path takes them, and the card lists D, E, C, B, D, C, A, B, E." width="100%"} An Eulerian path is a trail that uses every edge exactly once (nodes may repeat). It exists when the edges form one connected piece and, on an undirected graph, either every node has even degree (the path is then a closed circuit) or exactly two nodes have odd degree, which must be its two ends. On a directed graph, every node must have as many edges in as out, except possibly one start node with one extra out-edge and one end node with one extra in-edge. This is the classic "draw the figure without lifting your pen" problem, and it appears in route planning (snow ploughs, mail delivery, street inspection), DNA fragment assembly (de Bruijn graphs), and circuit design. `is_semieulerian()` and `is_eulerian()` test for the two cases; `eulerian_circuit()` returns closed trails only. As in those methods, isolated nodes are ignored. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [source]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str, None]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Where the path should start, as an integer ID or a string label. If the graph only has an open path, this must be one of its two possible ends. If `None` (default), a valid start is chosen. [edges]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `False` (default), return the path as node IDs. If `True`, return edge IDs, which are unambiguous when the graph has parallel edges. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[int] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The path as node IDs (one more than the number of edges; the first and last are the same for a circuit) or, with `edges=True`, edge IDs. `None` if no Eulerian path exists (from `source=`, if given). ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `source=` does not exist. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} The "house of Santa Claus" (a square with both diagonals and a roof) has exactly two odd nodes, the bottom corners, so it can be drawn in one stroke from one to the other: ::: {#74bdde8f .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec house = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["bl", "br", "tl", "tr", "roof"]) .add_edges([("bl", "br"), ("bl", "tl"), ("br", "tr"), ("tl", "tr"), ("tl", "roof"), ("tr", "roof"), ("bl", "tr"), ("br", "tl")]) ) [house.get_label_from_id(n) for n in house.eulerian_path()] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ['bl', 'br', 'tr', 'tl', 'bl', 'tr', 'roof', 'tl', 'br'] ``` ::: ::: Starting from a node that cannot be an end gives `None`: ::: {#d156cc68 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} house.eulerian_path(source="roof") is None ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` True ``` ::: :::
